Verse 1:1 of the Qur’an is the opening of **Surah Al-Fatiha** (The Opening), known as the **Basmala**:

**Arabic text:**
بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ

**Transliteration:**
*Bismillāhi r-raḥmāni r-raḥīm*

**English translation** (Sahih International):
*In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.*

(Other common renderings include: “In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.”)

**Arabic text (exact):**

قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ

**English translation** (Sahih International):

> Say, "He is Allah, [who is] One"

*(Or: "Say: He is Allah, the One.")*

This is the first verse of **Surah Al-Ikhlas** (Chapter 112), also known as *Surah At-Tawhid*.

This is **Ayat al-Kursi** (the Verse of the Throne), Surah Al-Baqarah (2:255).

**Exact Arabic text (Uthmani script):**

اللَّهُ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْحَيُّ الْقَيُّومُ ۚ لَا تَأْخُذُهُ سِنَةٌ وَلَا نَوْمٌ ۚ لَهُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ ۗ مَن ذَا الَّذِي يَشْفَعُ عِندَهُ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِهِ ۚ يَعْلَمُ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ ۖ وَلَا يُحِيطُونَ بِشَيْءٍ مِّنْ عِلْمِهِ إِلَّا بِمَا شَاءَ ۚ وَسِعَ كُرْسِيُّهُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ ۖ وَلَا يَئُودُهُ حِفْظُهُمَا ۚ وَهُوَ الْعَلِيُّ الْعَظِيمُ

**English translation** (Sahih International, with minor adjustments for clarity):

> Allah — there is no deity worthy of worship except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of [all] existence. Neither drowsiness overtakes Him nor sleep. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission? He knows what is [presently] before them and what will be after them, and they encompass not a thing of His knowledge except for what He wills. His Kursi extends over the heavens and the earth, and their preservation tires Him not. And He is the Most High, the Most Great.

*(Note: “Kursi” is often translated as “Footstool” in technical theological contexts, though some renderings use “Throne”; the verse emphasizes that it is vast enough to encompass the heavens and the earth.)*

Verse 36:1 is the opening of **Surah Ya-Sin** (Surah 36). It consists of the two disjointed Arabic letters **Ya** (ي) and **Sin** (س).

**Exact Arabic text:**
> **يس**

**Transliteration:** *Yā Sīn*

**English translation (common renderings):**
- **"Ya Sin"** (most literal, leaving the letters as they are, since they are among the *Muqatta'at* / disjointed letters whose precise meaning is known to God).
- Some translators render it interpretively as **"O Man"** (e.g., Sahih International: *"Ya, [O] man"*), though this is an interpretive reading rather than a literal translation of the letters themselves.

**Context:** The verse is immediately followed by verse 2: *"By the wise Qur'an..."* (وَالْقُرْآنِ الْحَكِيمِ). The letters *Ya Sin* are also the name of the Surah.

**Surah Al-Hujurat (49), Verse 12**

**Arabic (Uthmani script):**
يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اجْتَنِبُوا كَثِيرًا مِّنَ الظَّنِّ إِنَّ بَعْضَ الظَّنِّ إِثْمٌ ۖ وَلَا تَجَسَّسُوا وَلَا يَغْتَب بَّعْضُكُم بَعْضًا ۚ أَيُحِبُّ أَحَدُكُمْ أَن يَأْكُلَ لَحْمَ أَخِيهِ مَيْتًا فَكَرِهْتُمُوهُ ۚ وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ ۚ إِنَّ اللَّهَ تَوَّابٌ رَّحِيمٌ

**English translation (Sahih International):**
"O you who have believed, avoid much [negative] assumption. Indeed, some assumption is sin. And do not spy or backbite each other. Would one of you like to eat the flesh of his brother when dead? You would detest it. And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is Accepting of repentance and Merciful."

**Surah An-Nur (24:35)**

**Arabic text:**
اللَّهُ نُورُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ ۚ مَثَلُ نُورِهِ كَمِشْكَاةٍ فِيهَا مِصْبَاحٌ ۖ الْمِصْبَاحُ فِي زُجَاجَةٍ ۖ الزُّجَاجَةُ كَأَنَّهَا كَوْكَبٌ دُرِّيٌّ يُوقَدُ مِن شَجَرَةٍ مُّبَارَكَةٍ زَيْتُونَةٍ لَّا شَرْقِيَّةٍ وَلَا غَرْبِيَّةٍ يَكَادُ زَيْتُهَا يُضِيءُ وَلَوْ لَمْ تَمْسَسْهُ نَارٌ ۚ نُورٌ عَلَىٰ نُورٍ ۗ يَهْدِي اللَّهُ لِنُورِهِ مَن يَشَاءُ ۚ وَيَضْرِبُ اللَّهُ الْأَمْثَالَ لِلنَّاسِ ۗ وَاللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ

**English translation (Sahih International):**
"Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth. The example of His light is like a niche within which is a lamp, the lamp is within glass, the glass as if it were a pearly [white] star. It is lit from [the oil of] a blessed olive tree, neither of the east [only] nor of the west [only], whose oil would almost glow even if it had not been touched by fire. Light upon light. Allah guides to His light whom He wills. And Allah presents examples for the people, and Allah is Knowing of all things."

**Surah Al-ʿAṣr (103), verse 2**

**Arabic text:**
إِنَّ الْإِنسَانَ لَفِي خُسْرٍ

**English translation (Sahih International):**
"Indeed, mankind is in loss."

*(Context: The full chapter begins with the oath "By time, indeed mankind is in loss, except for those who have believed and done righteous deeds and advised each other to truth and advised each other to patience.")*

This is **Surah Luqman (31), verse 13**.

**Arabic text:**
وَإِذْ قَالَ لُقْمَانُ لِابْنِهِ وَهُوَ يَعِظُهُ يَا بُنَيَّ لَا تُشْرِكْ بِاللَّهِ ۚ إِنَّ الشِّرْكَ لَظُلْمٌ عَظِيمٌ

**English translation** (Sahih International):
> "And [mention] when Luqman said to his son while he was instructing him, 'O my son, do not associate partners with Allah. Indeed, association [with Him] is great injustice.'"

*(Other common renderings: "O my son! Do not associate partners with Allah. Verily, polytheism is a tremendous wrong indeed.")*

**Arabic text (Surah Al-Mujadila, 58:11):**

يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِذَا قِيلَ لَكُمْ تَفَسَّحُوا فِي الْمَجَالِسِ فَافْسَحُوا يَفْسَحِ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ ۖ وَإِذَا قِيلَ انشُزُوا فَانشُزُوا يَرْفَعِ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مِنكُمْ وَالَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْعِلْمَ دَرَجَاتٍ ۚ وَاللَّهُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرٌ

*(Standard Uthmani script; diacritics shown for clarity.)*

**English translation (Sahih International):**

“O you who have believed, when it is said to you, ‘Make room within the assemblies,’ then make room; Allah will make room for you. And when it is said, ‘Rise,’ then rise; Allah will raise those who have believed among you and those who have been given knowledge, by degrees. And Allah is Acquainted with what you do.”

*(Other common renderings: “Make space” / “Spread out” for *tafassaḥū*, and “Stand up” / “Rise up” for *unshuzū*.)*

This is **Surah Al-Ankabut (29:45)**.

**Arabic text:**
وَاتْلُ مَا أُوحِيَ إِلَيْكَ مِنَ الْكِتَابِ وَأَقِمِ الصَّلَاةَ ۚ إِنَّ الصَّلَاةَ تَنْهَىٰ عَنِ الْفَحْشَاءِ وَالْمُنكَرِ ۗ وَلَذِكْرُ اللَّهِ أَكْبَرُ ۗ وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ مَا تَصْنَعُونَ

**English translation (Sahih International):**
"And recite what has been revealed to you of the Book and establish prayer. Indeed, prayer prevents immorality and wrongdoing, and the remembrance of Allah is greater. And Allah knows that which you do."

**Surah Al-Mutaffifin (83), Verse 1**

**Arabic (Uthmani script):**
وَيْلٌ لِّلْمُطَفِّفِينَ

**Transliteration:**
*Waylun lil-muṭaffifīn*

**English translation (Sahih International):**
"Woe to the defrauders,"

**Other common renderings:**
- "Woe to those who give short measure!" (Pickthall)
- "Woe to the cheaters/short-changers!" (literal sense of *muṭaffifīn*)

This is the opening verse of the 83rd chapter of the Qur'an, *Surah Al-Mutaffifin* ("The Defrauders" or "Those Who Give Short Measure"), which condemns those who cheat in weights and measures.

**Surah Al-Ahqaf (46), Verse 9**

**Arabic text (Uthmani script):**
قُلْ مَا كُنْتُ بِدِيعًا مِّنَ الرُّسُلِ وَلَا أَدْرِي مَا يُفْعَلُ بِي وَلَا لَكُمْ ۖ إِنْ أَتَّبِعُ إِلَّا مَا يُوحَىٰ إِلَيَّ ۚ وَمَا أَنَا إِلَّا نَذِيرٌ مُّبِينٌ

**English translation (Sahih International):**
Say, "I am not an innovation among the messengers, nor do I know what will be done with me or with you. I only follow that which is revealed to me, and I am not but a clear warner."
